child_repository_rule: one standalone Git repository per company-appointed agent and canonical role
invariants: the parent owns lane baseline files only
a child repository owns all files below its own repository root
no file may be tracked by both parent and child repositories
the same local agent name in another jurisdiction is safe only when stable agent_id and appointment differ
repository location never grants appointment, delegation, release approval, run authorization, or effect authority
persona, provider profile, runtime host, and read territory do not determine accountable home
rollback: close or revert the candidate change
retain current lane and child repository layout
do not move, create, retire, or activate any child as part of rollback
acceptance_scenarios: parent baseline files are tracked by the parent and child roots are ignored
each child root is a distinct Git repository with no tracked-file overlap
a company appointment points to the child repository without deriving authority from the path
migration planning produces a reviewable no-apply diff and preserves child history
reversal_triggers: Git cannot enforce non-overlapping parent and child ownership
the selected layout requires authority to be inferred from paths
an accepted appointing-jurisdiction rule places SoftwareCo agents elsewhere
a migration would overwrite child-owned history or persona content
prohibited_authority_transfer: no appointment authority to the parent lane
no provider authority to SoftwareCo through import or placement
no release approval or run authorization from repository existence
no runtime or effect authority from the execution host
